_comment: Labeled test set for src/evaluate.py. expected_intent / expected_should_escalate are hand-authored ground truth (what a correct system should do), independent of this build's own rules, so evaluate.py measures the real gap between the two rather than grading the code against itself.

requests.request_text: Where is my order ORD-1003?
requests.note: clean status check

requests.request_text: Can you give me the status of my order ORD-1005?
requests.note: clean status check

requests.request_text: Has ORD-1002 shipped yet?
requests.note: clean status check

requests.request_text: When will ORD-1099 arrive? Track it please.
requests.note: invalid order id — should report not-found, not escalate

requests.request_text: I've been waiting forever, ORD-1003 better have shipped by now.
requests.note: indirect phrasing, no question mark — expected to be a hard case for the keyword rules

requests.request_text: where's my package? ORD-1010
requests.note: clean status check

requests.request_text: I'd like a refund for ORD-1001, it arrived damaged.
requests.note: damage claim bypasses expired window, amount under threshold

requests.request_text: Please refund ORD-1005, I changed my mind.
requests.note: within window, amount under threshold

requests.request_text: Can I get my money back for ORD-1009? I don't want it anymore.
requests.note: window long expired, no damage claim — needs human judgment

requests.request_text: Refund ORD-1004 please, the chair broke after a week.
requests.note: amount ($310) over auto-approval threshold

requests.request_text: I want a refund for ORD-1006, it's way too expensive, I don't need it.
requests.note: amount ($540) over auto-approval threshold

requests.request_text: Give me a refund for ORD-1002, wrong item was sent to me.
requests.note: amount ($189) over auto-approval threshold

requests.request_text: Refund request for ORD-1007, I ordered the wrong color.
requests.note: order still processing — nothing to refund yet, deterministic

requests.request_text: I'd like a refund for ORD-1010, item was defective right out of the box.
requests.note: defective claim, amount under threshold, within window anyway

requests.request_text: ORD-1008 stopped working after two days, I want to send it back.
requests.note: no refund-style keyword present — expected to be a hard case; amount ($112.40) is over threshold either way

requests.request_text: Order ORD-1003 arrived broken, need a refund ASAP!!
requests.note: customer claims delivery but backend data says order is still processing — system should trust backend data

requests.request_text: Please update my shipping address for ORD-1003 to 45 New Lane, Boston, MA.
requests.note: order still processing — eligible for address change

requests.request_text: My order ORD-1003 needs a new address: 22 Baker Street, Seattle, WA.
requests.note: colon-style phrasing instead of 'to' — expected to be a hard case for address extraction

requests.request_text: Change my address on ORD-1008 to 9 Elm Court, Denver, CO please.
requests.note: order already shipped — deterministic rejection, not escalation

requests.request_text: Please redirect my order ORD-1005 - new place is 5 Pine Ave, Chicago, IL
requests.note: order already delivered (deterministic rejection) and no literal 'to' before the address — a hard case on two axes
